events.extended_summary: More than 200 doctors have had their details sent in error to the Times newspaper The doctors' regulator the General Medical Council (GMC) has apologised after it mistakenly sent information about more than 220 doctors to a national newspaper. The information included summaries of complaints alleging antisemitism or Islamophobia against the doctors. For some of the medics involved, it was only when the GMC alerted them to the data breach that they discovered a complaint had been made about them. The GMC says it is "very sorry" for the incident and has reported itself to the Information Commissioner's Office. The GMC - an independent body that regulates doctors, physician associates and anaesthesia associates to protect patient safety - sent the information about 223 doctors to a journalist at the Times newspaper. While no names were revealed, GMC identification numbers were included, which would easily allow doctors to be found on
events.micro_summary: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper.
events.summary: Regulator mistakenly sent complaints about doctors to newspaper. Medical professionals have called for an inquiry after the regulator sent details concerning 223 doctors to a national newspaper journalist "in error".

events.extended_summary: A senior United States Navy official has claimed that insurance costs for commercial ships crossing the Strait of Hormuz have soared to $64m for a single transit, highlighting the enormous economic toll of the US-Israeli war on Iran. Acting US Navy Secretary Hung Cao made the remarks during a Senate Armed Services Committee confirmation hearing on Tuesday, as lawmakers questioned the cost of the war and its impact on freedom of navigation. After the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran on February 28, Iran in effect closed the strait, allowing only some ships to pass while targeting those it says are unauthorised. This has raised the risks for shipping in the strait exponentially and caused severe shortages of oil, gas, fertiliser and other essential products from Gulf producers usually shipped via this route. events.micro_summary: US official says Hormuz insurance hits $64m: Is the strait really open?

events.extended_summary: An American newlywed was left fighting for his life after a hippopotamus attack in Botswana, and says he only survived because his wife punched it until it let him go. Samuel McKee, 31, and his wife Anna were on their honeymoon in the Okavango Delta in September last year when their wildlife excursion turned into a fight for survival. The Washington state couple were travelling through the delta in a traditional mokoro canoe when their guide had pointed out a mother hippo and her calves and warned them to avoid the area, the couple told Newsweek. But the animal suddenly charged, tossing the husband and his wife into the water. “Then the hippo hit. It grabbed me around the torso and pinned me to the bottom of the swamp,” Samuel McKee told Newsweek. “What I remember most was the force. It was more force than I’d ever experienced in my
events.micro_summary: Horror as raging hippo rips open groom on honeymoon before bride punches beast in face.
events.summary: Horror as raging hippo rips open groom on honeymoon before bride punches beast in face. A newlywed woman saved her husband's life after punching a hippopotamus in the head as the animal mauled him during their honeymoon safari in Botswana.

events.extended_summary: A fractious summit in Dublin concluded last Friday without agreement on who would speak for Europe in forthcoming talks to end the Russian invasion of Ukraine. Jared Kushner, representing President Trump alongside Steve Witkoff, stated that Europeans agreeing on a single figure would be a greater achievement than securing a place at the table. Prior to the talks, some European commentators and Estonia's foreign ministry argued that Kaja Kallas, the EU's High Representative for Foreign and Security Affairs, was the only person with authority to represent Europe strategically. Moscow had previously stated it would never discuss anything with Kallas and would wait until she left office, though by Saturday Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia would not set terms about European personnel in advance. Former president Dmitri Medvedev nevertheless called Kallas stupid and said nobody wanted her. Estonia, Kallas's home country, is considered the EU member most exposed to potential Russian aggression.
events.micro_summary: A Dublin summit concluded Friday without agreement on who will represent Europe in Ukraine peace talks.
events.summary: A fractious Dublin summit concluded Friday without consensus on Europe's representative for talks to end the Russian invasion of Ukraine, as Moscow initially rejected EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas but later softened its stance on personnel conditions.

events.extended_summary: Pete Hegseth met Venezuela's interim president at the presidential palace The United States and Venezuela have re-established military ties less than a year after US forces seized the then-leader of the South American country, Nicolás Maduro, in a raid on the capital, Caracas. The interim government led by Delcy Rodríguez, Maduro's former vice-president, signed a military co-operation agreement with US Secretary of Defence Pete Hegseth on Wednesday. Few details about the deal have been released so far but Hegseth said that Venezuela had "gone from our most aggressive regional threat to a compliant security partner" in less than 12 months. Interim President Rodríguez said the deal would help confront "common threats". Military co-operation between the two countries was terminated in 2005 by Hugo Chávez, Venezuela's left-wing president at the time. Chávez alleged that US military personnel sent to Venezuela to train their counterparts had made disparaging remarks about his government.
events.micro_summary: Venezuela signs military deal with US less than a year after Maduro's removal.
events.summary: Venezuela signs military deal with US less than a year after Maduro's removal. United States Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has announced a new cooperation agreement with Venezuela’s interim government to facilitate military cooperation between the two countries.

events.extended_summary: The International Court of Justice ruled by a nine-to-six majority that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority during a 2017 military campaign. The court found that the military junta had the intent to destroy a substantial part of the Rohingya population, killing 1.2 percent of the target group and displacing more than 700,000 people to Bangladesh. This marks the first time the world court has found a state responsible for genocide. The judges determined that no single smoking gun was required, as circumstantial evidence sufficiently established genocidal intent. The ruling ends a seven-year legal battle and sets a precedent for future genocide claims. Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh celebrated the verdict, with survivors expressing relief and hope for future generations.
events.micro_summary: International Court of Justice rules Myanmar committed genocide against Rohingya by nine-to-six vote.
events.summary: The International Court of Justice ruled nine to six that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority during a 2017 campaign that displaced over 700,000 people, finding intent to destroy a substantial part of the population.

events.extended_summary: Ukrainian forces employed advanced drone tactics to strike Russian military assets in multiple operations across the front. The 237th Unmanned Systems Battalion deployed heavy fixed-wing drones, normally reserved for distant middle strikes against supply lines, against vehicles rolling toward the gray zone west of Huliaipole and in attacks toward Kramatorsk. On 13 November, the 1st Azov Corps defeated a Russian column that crossed the foggy gray zone from Shakhove, presumably using thermal-camera drones. Separately, the 1st Separate Assault Regiment used Darts fixed-wing drones to hit seven vehicles gathering in Razine. Meanwhile, the 33rd Brigade destroyed a BM-21 Grad multiple-launch rocket system with 40 launch tubes, several ground robotic vehicles, and an infantry shelter hidden in an autumn forest.
events.micro_summary: Ukrainian drone units destroyed Russian vehicles and a rocket system using heavy fixed-wing drones and thermal cameras.
events.summary: Ukrainian drone battalions used heavy fixed-wing drones to destroy Russian vehicles near Kramatorsk and a BM-21 Grad system in a forest.

events.extended_summary: A former Australian cricketer has stated that the entire team on the 2018 South Africa tour knew about the use of sandpaper on the ball, contradicting the previous account that only three players were involved. He admitted that during Cricket Australia's 2018 investigation, he did not provide a complete account, withholding details about when the sandpaper use began, how long it continued, and the involvement of others. He said he carried this burden for eight years. Cricket Australia has announced an independent forum for all those on the 2018 tour, which he plans to attend. He cited the release of Usman Khawaja's autobiography and a press conference by captain Pat Cummins as catalysts for speaking out, saying his career has been destroyed and he has not played for Australia since Justin Langer was coach.
events.micro_summary: A former Australian cricketer admits the entire 2018 South Africa tour team knew about ball-tampering.
events.summary: A former Australian cricketer has admitted the entire 2018 South Africa tour team knew about sandpaper ball-tampering, not just three players, and that he withheld details during the investigation. Cricket Australia is opening an independent forum for tour participants.

events.extended_summary: Mauricio Pochettino has vowed to "change things" at Old Trafford in a confident first interview as Manchester United boss. The Argentine arrived following his departure from the United States national team, tasked with improving United's fortunes after a dismal start to the season. United sit 18th in the Premier League ahead of Pochettino's first game in charge, Sunday's trip to Liverpool at Anfield. Pochettino believes it would be a mistake to focus solely on United's current predicament, insisting the club's potential rather than its problems must be the starting point for his tenure. He stated the focus must be on seeing the potential of the club and acting to change things across all areas to recover the feeling of winning. Pochettino emphasized his priority is to create an environment where players can express themselves and rediscover the feeling of being winners through hard work.
events.micro_summary: Mauricio Pochettino vows to change things as Manchester United boss with club 18th in Premier League.
events.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has vowed to change things at Old Trafford in his first interview as Manchester United boss, with the club 18th in the Premier League ahead of Sunday's trip to Liverpool.

events.extended_summary: Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey was deactivated for the team's weekend game at Carolina following controversial remarks on his podcast. During a segment, the 30-year-old veteran said Baltimore is 'best at making criminals,' prompting an apology Wednesday. Baltimore Mayor Brandon Scott stated a verbal apology was 'not enough' and invited Humphrey to meet with community members who have re-entered society. First-year head coach Jesse Minter announced the one-game deactivation Thursday, stating Humphrey was sent home and would not practice, emphasizing that the comments did not reflect the team. The Ravens, currently on a five-game losing streak after a 4-1 start, have lost quarterbacks Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley to injuries. Humphrey, a 2017 first-round pick and four-time Pro Bowler, has faced criticism from fans during the team's struggles.
events.micro_summary: Ravens deactivate cornerback Marlon Humphrey for one game after 'criminals' podcast remark.
events.summary: Baltimore Ravens cornerback Marlon Humphrey was deactivated for the team's game at Carolina after saying on a podcast that Baltimore is best at making 'criminals.' Coach Jesse Minter announced the one-game deactivation Thursday, sending Humphrey home.

events.extended_summary: Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, a 42-year-old technology teacher at Wesley International Academy, died on October 12 after being flung from the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia in Austell. An autopsy determined he died from blunt force injuries after falling onto the roof of a park building, sustaining extensive injuries to his legs, arms, torso, neck, and head. He was seated next to his niece when he fell, striking several other guests before landing. The 5'9", 301-pound man was visiting the park to celebrate his niece's birthday. Following the incident, Six Flags closed nine roller coasters including Goliath, later keeping eight additional rides at five other parks closed out of caution. CEO John Reilly announced that seat belts would be added to the Goliath ride and similar coasters. The Cobb County Police Department launched an investigation into the death.
events.micro_summary: School teacher Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem died from blunt force trauma after falling from Six Flags' Goliath coaster.
events.summary: Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, 42, died October 12 after being ejected from the Goliath roller coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia, landing on a building roof and suffering blunt force injuries. Six Flags closed the ride and added seat belts.

events.extended_summary: At a Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin, the UK announced a £260 million support package for Ukraine that includes 1,000 long-range strike drones capable of flying 625 miles and carrying heavier warheads to target military production facilities, with 80 percent of the funding spent domestically. Simultaneously, the UK and Norway committed over £100 million to jointly fund two advanced 30-metre fast attack boats built in the UK, providing frigate-like offensive and air defence capabilities to protect the Black Sea Grain Corridor and secure trade routes. The vessels will strengthen Ukraine's naval capability and apply pressure on Russia, while both nations also agreed to deepen cooperation on defensive artificial intelligence for the battlefield.
events.micro_summary: UK and Norway pledge two attack boats and 1,000 drones to Ukraine at Berlin summit.
events.summary: At a Berlin meeting of the Coalition of the Willing, the UK announced a £260m package including 1,000 long-range strike drones for Ukraine, while jointly funding two advanced fast attack boats with Norway worth over £100 million.

events.extended_summary: The MV Mwanza, a 306ft vessel carrying 1,200 passengers, crashed into Bismarck Rock in Tanzania's Lake Victoria at around 10:30am on Wednesday. The ship had narrowly missed a passenger ferry inbound from Sengerema moments earlier when the ferry captain reversed, causing the MV Mwanza to strike the rock formation. Footage showed the vessel mounting the rocks before crashing back down into the lake, with black smoke erupting from the ship, which then reversed into open water. Witness Bakari Mwigeli stated the ferry captain's swift actions prevented greater damage. The vessel, which entered service this year as the largest ferry on Lake Victoria, was reportedly undergoing sea trials with stakeholders on board. No one was injured in the incident, and local authorities have launched an investigation.
events.micro_summary: MV Mwanza cruise ship carrying 1,200 passengers crashed into Bismarck Rock in Lake Victoria with no injuries reported.
events.summary: The MV Mwanza, a 306ft vessel carrying 1,200 passengers, crashed into Bismarck Rock in Tanzania's Lake Victoria around 10:30am Wednesday after narrowly missing a ferry. No one was injured and authorities launched an investigation.

events.extended_summary: Adam McSweeney, 18, was stabbed at Kent train station on Lower Glanmire Road, Cork, at about 1.30pm on Tuesday. Paramedics treated him at the scene before he was taken in critical condition to Cork University Hospital, where he died three hours later. Timothy Miller, 18, appeared at Cork District Court on Thursday charged with McSweeney's murder. When charged, Miller replied, 'This is self-defence.' Judge David Waters remanded him in custody to appear by video-link on November 25th, noting bail is not available on a murder charge at district court level. A 16-year-old arrested in the same investigation was released without charge, with a file to be prepared for the Director of Public Prosecutions. Gardaí have appealed for witnesses to come forward. A post-mortem is scheduled for Wednesday at Cork University Hospital.
events.micro_summary: Adam McSweeney, 18, was stabbed to death in Cork; Timothy Miller, 18, remanded in custody on murder charge.
events.summary: Adam McSweeney, 18, died after being stabbed at Kent train station in Cork on Tuesday. Timothy Miller, 18, was charged with his murder and remanded in custody at Cork District Court on Thursday.

events.extended_summary: KKR announced the acquisition of a minority stake in Gentari Renewables India, the Indian renewable energy subsidiary of clean energy solutions provider Gentari, which was launched in 2022 by Malaysian integrated oil and gas company Petronas. The platform has approximately 8 GW of operating, under-construction and contracted renewable energy capacity across solar, wind, hybrid and battery energy storage projects serving commercial, industrial and government customers. The transaction provides growth capital to support expansion in India, which aims to reach 500 GW of installed renewable energy capacity by 2030 and has approved targets to reduce economy-wide emissions intensity by 47% and achieve 60% of electric power capacity from non-fossil sources by 2035. Under the agreement, Gentari retains strategic oversight and full operational control of the Indian platform. KKR Partner Hardik Shah stated that India's growing demand for reliable power creates significant need for continued energy infrastructure investment, while Gentari CEO Sushil Purohit said the partnership supports continued expansion of the renewable energy business in India.
events.micro_summary: KKR acquired a minority stake in Gentari Renewables India, which has approximately 8 GW of renewable capacity.
events.summary: KKR acquired a minority stake in Gentari Renewables India, the Indian subsidiary of Petronas-backed Gentari, which operates approximately 8 GW of renewable energy capacity, to provide growth capital for expansion while Gentari retains operational control.

events.extended_summary: Ramayana: Rise of the Legend has completed 14 days in theatres, crossing Rs 1,500 crore worldwide and Rs 1,000 crore gross in India. The film starring Ranbir Kapoor, Sai Pallavi and Yash reached a worldwide total of Rs 1,519.05 crore, making it the fastest Indian movie to achieve the milestone and the fifth Indian film overall to cross Rs 1,500 crore globally. Domestically, it collected Rs 1,009.05 crore gross and Rs 844.40 crore nett, with overseas earnings at Rs 510 crore, becoming the sixth Indian film and third Bollywood film to enter the domestic Rs 1,000 crore gross club. On Day 14, it earned Rs 23.20 crore nett. The Nitesh Tiwari directorial also set records for highest single-day BookMyShow ticket sales with 16.60 lakh tickets and the biggest worldwide IMAX opening for an Indian film at approximately $6 million.
events.micro_summary: Ramayana becomes fastest Indian film to cross Rs 1,500 crore worldwide in just 14 days.
events.summary: Ramayana: Rise of the Legend crossed Rs 1,500 crore worldwide and Rs 1,000 crore gross in India in 14 days, becoming the fastest Indian film to reach the global milestone and the third Bollywood film in the domestic club.

events.extended_summary: India and Egypt are expanding bilateral cooperation in digital governance, emerging technologies, and administrative capacity building. Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh highlighted India's governance innovations and civil services framework while interacting with a delegation of 25 Deputy Governors from Egypt participating in the first Special Capacity-Building Programme on Smart Governance in New Delhi. Singh described India's administrative system as one of the world's largest civil services frameworks, the "steel frame of governance," and stressed two-way learning in capacity-building programmes. The countries elevated their relationship to a Strategic Partnership in June 2023. Bilateral trade reached US$7.26 billion in FY 2021–22 and stood at US$4.8 billion in FY 2024–25. More than 500 Indian companies are registered in Egypt with investments exceeding US$4.5 billion, and over 1,500 Egyptian officials have benefited from Indian Technical and Economic Cooperation programmes.
events.micro_summary: India and Egypt deepen ties in digital governance with 25 Egyptian Deputy Governors training in New Delhi.
events.summary: India and Egypt are expanding cooperation in digital governance and emerging technologies, with Union Minister Dr. Jitendra Singh hosting 25 Egyptian Deputy Governors for a capacity-building programme in New Delhi, building on their Strategic Partnership and $4.8 billion bilateral trade.

events.extended_summary: Japan and India agreed to enhance their military and arms industry cooperation, including allowing Japanese troops to conduct live-fire missile training at Indian firing ranges in future joint drills. Defense and foreign ministers from both nations met Thursday in Tokyo for a "two-plus-two" meeting. Japanese Defense Minister Shinjiro Koizumi and Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi joined Indian counterparts Rajnath Singh and S. Jaishankar. The agreement proceeds under a "design with Japan, make in India" framework. Japan, an island nation with limited space for missile tests, needs partners to provide facilities for live-fire drills essential to improving missile capability. The ministers also agreed to promote cooperation in defense equipment and technology and accelerate negotiations for transferring the Japanese naval radio antenna UNICORN to India. They reaffirmed deepening cooperation in air and maritime security, information sharing, search and rescue operations, naval shipbuilding and artificial intelligence.
events.micro_summary: Japan and India agreed Thursday to enhance military ties and allow Japanese live-fire missile training at Indian ranges.

events.summary: Japan and India agreed to enhance military and arms industry cooperation, including allowing Japanese troops to conduct live-fire missile training at Indian firing ranges during future joint drills at a Tokyo meeting Thursday.

events.extended_summary: Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju criticized Leader of Opposition Rahul Gandhi for describing India's economy as dead and alleging vote theft during his visit to the United States. Rijiju cited assessments by the International Monetary Fund and World Bank recognizing India as the world's fastest-growing major economy, contrasting this with Gandhi's remarks. He rejected claims that democracy does not exist in India, arguing that Gandhi's ability to openly protest and criticize Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP demonstrates freedom of expression. Rijiju also referenced World Bank data indicating over 50 crore people were lifted out of poverty between 2011 and 2023. He accused Gandhi of making inaccurate statements abroad that damage his own political standing and that of the Opposition, stating that such remarks on foreign soil are shameful for the Leader of Opposition.
events.micro_summary: Union Minister Kiren Rijiju criticized Rahul Gandhi for calling India's economy dead during his US visit.
events.summary: Union Minister Kiren Rijiju rebuked Rahul Gandhi for calling India's economy dead and questioning democracy during his US visit, citing IMF and World Bank recognition of India as the fastest-growing major economy and over 50 crore people lifted from poverty.

events.extended_summary: The Karnataka government announced India's first government Sports Technology Centre of Excellence at the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit, which concluded on Thursday, November 19. The state signed a Letter of Intent with Amagi Media Labs Limited to establish the facility in Bengaluru, structured around three pillars: Core Technology and Research Areas, Athlete Development, and Cross-Cutting Ecosystem Enablers. The government will provide seed funding and infrastructure while industry professionals manage operations under a model described as 'run by the industry, for the industry, for the sports fraternity.' The sports ecosystem is expected to grow by 12–15% in coming years. The government also announced a shared CSR Circularity Ecosystem with SoulAce Consulting and an AI Lab.
events.micro_summary: Karnataka announced India's first government Sports Technology Centre of Excellence at the Bengaluru Tech Summit.
events.summary: At the 29th Bengaluru Tech Summit, Karnataka announced India's first government Sports Technology Centre of Excellence, signing a Letter of Intent with Amagi Media Labs to establish the facility in Bengaluru with three operational pillars.

events.extended_summary: Karnataka hosts 1,088 of India's 2,117 Global Capability Centres, representing 51% of the national total and employing 829,000 people, including 111,000 AI/ML professionals who constitute 43% of India's GCC AI/ML workforce. The state's GCCs score 1.12x the national average on AI maturity and operate 120-plus dedicated AI/ML centres of excellence, nearly half of India's 250-plus. Between FY2021 and FY2026E, Karnataka attracted 217 of India's 510 new GCCs, including 46 of 89 new Global 2000 centres. Bengaluru accounts for 44% of India's senior AI-leadership GCC job postings, 6.4 times the average of other tier-1 cities. The state also holds 29% of India's AI startups and 60,000 of the country's 110,000 technical engineering leaders.
events.micro_summary: Karnataka hosts 51% of India's 2,117 GCCs and 43% of its AI/ML talent with 1.12x AI maturity.
events.summary: Karnataka hosts 51% of India's 2,117 GCCs, employing 1.11 lakh AI/ML professionals and scoring 1.12x the national AI maturity average, with 69% of its GCCs maintaining dedicated AI budgets.

events.extended_summary: Bengaluru India’s aerospace, defence and space industry needs to move beyond isolated artificial intelligence (AI) experiments towards integrated, production-ready applications, with stronger data infrastructure, engineering capabilities and skilled manpower, as suggested by a report released at the Bengaluru Tech Summit. The report, titled ‘Intelligent by Design: AI Adoption in India’s Aerospace, Defence and Space Industry’, brought out by TiE Bangalore and the Aerospace Industry Association of India (AIA), identified AI as a significant opportunity to improve engineering productivity, manufacturing efficiency, maintenance and operational performance. However, it cautions that adoption across the sector remains uneven, with significant differences in technological maturity, investment capacity and organisational readiness. events.extended_summary: India and Japan agreed to strengthen their defence partnership during the fourth 2+2 ministerial meeting in Tokyo. Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar met Japanese counterparts Toshimitsu Motegi and Shinjiro Koizumi. They signed a Letter of Intent allowing the Japan Ground Self-Defence Force to conduct live-fire training with surface-to-ship missiles at Indian firing ranges for the first time. The nations set February 2027 as the target for transferring UNICORN communication system technology to enhance Indian Navy warship stealth. They agreed to expand research cooperation in advanced missile technologies, enhance joint exercises including 'Veer Guardian 26', and coordinate Indo-Pacific initiatives. Both reaffirmed commitment to a free, open, rules-based order, respect for sovereignty, and peaceful dispute resolution while opposing unilateral status quo changes.
events.micro_summary: India and Japan signed a letter of intent for first-time live-fire missile training by Japanese forces in India.
events.summary: India and Japan agreed during their 2+2 ministerial dialogue in Tokyo to strengthen defence ties, including first-time live-fire training for Japan's Ground Self-Defence Force in India and technology transfer of the UNICORN system by February 2027.
